text: How long a medicine stays active in the body varies widely and determines redosing timing: a few minutes (e.g. Oxytocin — a second dose can follow about 30 minutes later); about 1 hour (e.g. Calmagine, Analgin); about 12 hours (e.g. Ampidexalone, Biocolistine — inject again in the evening if the first dose was in the morning); about 1 day (e.g. Septotryl, Frecortyl); about 2 days (e.g. Tolfedine, Longamox); about 3 days (e.g. Remacycline, Longicine); and over 7 days (e.g. Iron Dextran). For injection, match syringe volume to the dose needed (a 20 ml syringe cannot accurately measure 1 ml, and a 10 ml syringe means splitting a 30 ml dose into 3 injections); match needle length to the injection site — for intramuscular injection in a large sow, neck fat can exceed 30 mm, so a needle of at least 40 mm is needed to actually reach muscle; and match needle diameter to the product — oily, viscous long-acting products need a larger needle to inject smoothly and quickly. For oral powder dosing without a mixer: dilute the medicine step by step for even distribution — e.g. mix 100 g first into 1 kg of raw material, then that mixture into 5 kg, then finally into 50 kg of feed.
